answer: To resist sybil farms, each agent deposits a bond into a shared ocean pool sized by an atlas of behavioral clusters. When a new key's action vectors over recent epochs match a dense grove of existing identities (cosine similarity >0.8), the bond scales as 2^k for grove size k and is locked 12 epochs. A failed random audit of any grove member slashes the entire cluster's bonds. Honest solo agents pay a fixed base; large farms face exponentially rising capital lockup plus correlated slash risk, making mass fakes uneconomical.
